steps.title: Run keyword and topic research
steps.description: Utilize the OpenAI API to generate a list of relevant content topics based on specific keywords. This step involves clustering the topics according to search intent to create a comprehensive content strategy.
steps.technical_explanation: This step acts as the initial data generation phase, consuming keywords as input and producing clustered topics as output. The OpenAI API endpoint used is '/v1/chat/completions', with a POST method. Required headers include 'Authorization' for Bearer Token Authentication and 'Content-Type' for application/json. The request payload must contain the model and messages, while the response will include choices with generated content. Edge cases include handling rate limits and ensuring the response structure contains the expected keys.
steps.code_snippet:
import json
import urllib.request

def fetch_topics(keywords):
    url = 'https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions'
    headers = {
        'Authorization': 'Bearer YOUR_OPENAI_API_KEY',
        'Content-Type': 'application/json'
    }
    data = json.dumps({
        'model': 'gpt-4o-mini',
        'messages': [{'role': 'user', 'content': f'Generate topics for: {keywords}'}]
    }).encode('utf-8')
    request = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, headers=headers)
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request) as response:
        result = json.loads(response.read())
    return [item['message']['content'] for item in result['choices']]

topics = fetch_topics('SEO strategies')

import json
import urllib.request

def insert_topics(topics):
    url = 'https://YOUR_SUPABASE_URL/rest/v1/topics'
    headers = {
        'apikey': 'YOUR_SUPABASE_KEY',
        'Authorization': 'Bearer YOUR_SUPABASE_KEY',
        'Content-Type': 'application/json',
        'Prefer': 'return=representation'
    }
    for topic in topics:
        data = json.dumps({'topic': topic, 'status': 'pending'}).encode('utf-8')
        request = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, headers=headers)
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request) as response:
            if response.status not in (200, 201, 204):
                raise Exception('Failed to insert topic')

insert_topics(topics)

import json
import urllib.request

def publish_content(approved_drafts):
    url = 'https://<your-n8n-instance>/webhook/publish'
    headers = {'Content-Type': 'application/json'}
    data = json.dumps({'drafts': approved_drafts}).encode('utf-8')

import os

import os
import json

def chunk_document(file_path, chunk_size=500):
    with open(file_path, 'r') as file:
        content = file.read()
    chunks = [content[i:i+chunk_size] for i in range(0, len(content), chunk_size)]
    return chunks

document_path = './documents/doc1.txt'
chunks = chunk_document(document_path)

with open('./cleaned_chunks.json', 'w') as outfile:
    json.dump(chunks, outfile)

result = chunk_document()

import json

API_KEY = '<COHERE_API_KEY>'
headers = {
    'Authorization': f'Bearer {API_KEY}',
    'Content-Type': 'application/json'
}

def generate_embedding(text_chunk):
    data = json.dumps({'texts': [text_chunk]}).encode('utf-8')
    request = urllib.request.Request('https://api.cohere.ai/embed', data=data, headers=headers)

with open('./cleaned_chunks.json', 'r') as infile:

import json
import urllib.request

API_KEY = 'your_openai_api_key'

def generate_translations(source_content, target_language):
    url = 'https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions'
    headers = {
        'Authorization': f'Bearer {API_KEY}',
        'Content-Type': 'application/json'
    }
    payload = json.dumps({
        'model': 'gpt-4o-mini',
        'messages': [{'role': 'user', 'content': f'Translate the following text to {target_language}: {source_content}'}]
    }).encode('utf-8')
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=payload, headers=headers)
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as response:
        return json.loads(response.read())['choices'][0]['message']['content']

translations = [generate_translations(text, 'es') for text in source_content]

result = generate_translations()

import http.server
import json

class WebhookHandler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        content_length = int(self.headers['Content-Length'])
        post_data = self.rfile.read(content_length)
        payload = json.loads(post_data)
        print('Received webhook:', payload)
        self.send_response(200)
        self.end_headers()

server = http.server.HTTPServer(('localhost', 8000), WebhookHandler)
print('Starting server on port 8000')
server.serve_forever()

steps.code_snippet:
import json

# Define the function to normalize and deduplicate leads

def normalize_and_deduplicate(prospects):
    seen = set()  # Set to track seen entries
    normalized = []  # List to store normalized leads
    for prospect in prospects:
        normalized_email = prospect['email'].lower()  # Normalize email to lowercase
        if normalized_email not in seen:
            seen.add(normalized_email)  # Add to seen set
            normalized.append(prospect)  # Append normalized prospect
    return normalized  # Return the list of normalized leads

# Execute the function
normalized_leads = normalize_and_deduplicate(prospects)

result = normalize_and_deduplicate()

import json
import urllib.request

# Define the function to enrich company information
def enrich_company_info(leads):
    enriched_leads = []  # List to store enriched leads
    for lead in leads:
        prompt = f'Provide company details for {lead["company_name"]}'  # Create prompt
        url = 'https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions'  # OpenAI API endpoint
        headers = {'Authorization': 'Bearer YOUR_OPENAI_API_KEY', 'Content-Type': 'application/json'}  # Set headers
        data = json.dumps({'model': 'gpt-4o-mini', 'messages': [{'role': 'user', 'content': prompt}]})  # Prepare request payload
        request = urllib.request.Request(url, data.encode('utf-8'), headers)  # Create request
        response = urllib.request.urlopen(request)  # Send request
        result = json.loads(response.read())  # Parse response
        company_info = result['choices'][0]['message']['content']  # Extract company info
        lead['company_info'] = company_info  # Add info to lead
        enriched_leads.append(lead)  # Append enriched lead
    return enriched_leads  # Return enriched leads

# Execute the function
enriched_leads = enrich_company_info(normalized_leads)

import json
import urllib.request

def analyze_sentiment(mentions):
    url = 'https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions'
    headers = {'Authorization': 'Bearer YOUR_OPENAI_API_KEY', 'Content-Type': 'application/json'}
    records = []
    for mention in mentions:
        prompt = f'Analyze the sentiment of the following text: {mention}'
        data = json.dumps({'model': 'gpt-4o-mini', 'messages': [{'role': 'user', 'content': prompt}]})
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, data.encode('utf-8'), headers)
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as response:
            content = json.loads(response.read())['choices'][0]['message']['content']
            sentiment = float(content)
            records.append({'text': mention, 'sentiment': sentiment})
    return records

analyzed = analyze_sentiment(mentions)

steps.code_snippet:
import json
import urllib.request
import statistics


def alert_on_spikes(analyzed):
    sentiments = [record['sentiment'] for record in analyzed]
    mean = statistics.mean(sentiments)
    stdev = statistics.stdev(sentiments)
    threshold = 2.0  # Define z-score threshold for spikes
    for sentiment in sentiments:
        z_score = (sentiment - mean) / stdev
        if z_score >= threshold:
            send_alert(sentiment)


def send_alert(sentiment):
    url = 'YOUR_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL'
    data = json.dumps({'text': f'Sentiment spike detected: {sentiment}'})
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data.encode('utf-8'), headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as response:
        if response.status != 200:
            raise Exception('Failed to send alert')

        normalized.append({'name': name, 'domain': domain})
    return normalized

import json
import urllib.request

def create_table():
    url = "https://your-supabase-url/rest/v1/rpc/create_table"
    headers = {
        "apikey": "your-api-key",
        "Authorization": "Bearer your-jwt-token",
        "Content-Type": "application/json"
    }
    data = {
        "table_name": "locations",
        "columns": [
            {"name": "id", "type": "SERIAL", "primary_key": True},
            {"name": "name", "type": "VARCHAR(255)", "not_null": True},
            {"name": "address", "type": "VARCHAR(255)", "not_null": True},
            {"name": "city", "type": "VARCHAR(100)", "not_null": True},
            {"name": "state", "type": "VARCHAR(100)", "not_null": True},
            {"name": "zip_code", "type": "VARCHAR(10)", "not_null": True},
            {"name": "phone_number", "type": "VARCHAR(15)"},
            {"name": "email", "type": "VARCHAR(100)"},
            {"name": "created_at", "type": "TIMESTAMP", "default": "CURRENT_TIMESTAMP"}
        ]
    }
    request = urllib.request.Request(url, data=json.dumps(data).encode(), headers=headers)
    response = urllib.request.urlopen(request)
    return response.read()

result = create_table()
steps.technical_explanation: The SQL schema defines a table named 'locations' with fields for storing location-specific data. The 'id' field is a primary key, and 'created_at' automatically logs the timestamp of record creation. This setup ensures data integrity and easy retrieval for page generation.

import json

import urllib.parse
import datetime

def fetch_metrics():
    url = "http://example.com/api/metrics"
    response = urllib.request.urlopen(url)
    data = json.loads(response.read())
    return data

def analyze_metrics(metrics):
    threshold = 100
    for metric in metrics:
        if metric['metric_name'] == 'page_load_time' and metric['avg_value'] > threshold:
            update_website_settings('high')

def update_website_settings(optimization_level):
    url = "http://example.com/api/website_settings"
    data = json.dumps({"optimization_level": optimization_level}).encode('utf-8')
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, method='PUT')
    req.add_header('Content-Type', 'application/json')
    urllib.request.urlopen(req)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    metrics = fetch_metrics()
    analyze_metrics(metrics)

steps.code_snippet:
import urllib.request
import json

def fetch_issues(github_token, repo_owner, repo_name):
    url = f'https://api.github.com/repos/{repo_owner}/{repo_name}/issues'
    req = urllib.request.Request(url)
    req.add_header('Authorization', f'token {github_token}')
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as response:
        issues = json.loads(response.read())
    return issues

# Example usage

steps.code_snippet:
import json
import os
import subprocess

def run_command(command):
    process = subprocess.Popen(command, shell=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
    stdout, stderr = process.communicate()
    return stdout, stderr

def main():
    if os.getenv('CI') == 'true':
        print("Running CI/CD Pipeline")
        run_command("npm install")
        stdout, stderr = run_command("npm test")
        if stderr:
            print("Tests failed:", stderr.decode())
            return
        print("Tests passed:", stdout.decode())
        run_command("npm run deploy")
    else:
        print("Not in CI environment")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
steps.technical_explanation: GitHub Actions uses YAML configuration files to define workflows. The 'on' key specifies triggers, such as pushes to the main branch. import json
import http.client

def create_appwrite_project(endpoint, api_key, project_name):
    conn = http.client.HTTPSConnection(endpoint)
    payload = json.dumps({"name": project_name})
    headers = {
        'X-Appwrite-Project': api_key,
        'Content-Type': 'application/json'
    }
    conn.request("POST", "/v1/projects", payload, headers)
    res = conn.getresponse()
    data = res.read()
    return json.loads(data)

# Usage
# create_appwrite_project('appwrite.io', '<YOUR_API_KEY>', 'my-appwrite-project')

steps.technical_explanation: Use the Slack API to create a webhook that listens for messages from your social media channels. The endpoint for posting messages is https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage. Ensure to handle errors by checking the response status and logging any issues.
steps.code_snippet:
import json
import urllib.request

slack_webhook_url = 'https://example.com/slack-webhook'
data = {'text': 'New post from social media!'}
headers = {'Content-Type': 'application/json'}

request = urllib.request.Request(slack_webhook_url, data=json.dumps(data).encode('utf-8'), headers=headers)
response = urllib.request.urlopen(request)
response_data = response.read().decode('utf-8')
print(response_data)
if response.status != 200:
    print('Error sending message to Slack')

steps.title: Process Data with Google Sheets API
steps.description: Automatically log collected social media data into Google Sheets using API triggers to update sheets with new entries. This allows for organized data storage and easy access for analysis.
steps.technical_explanation: Use the Google Sheets API to append new rows of data to a specified spreadsheet. The endpoint for appending data is https://sheets.googleapis.com/v4/spreadsheets/{spreadsheetId}/values/{range}:append. Ensure to include the correct authorization token in the headers.
steps.code_snippet:
import json
import urllib.request

spreadsheet_id = 'YOUR_SPREADSHEET_ID'
range_name = 'Sheet1!A1'
data = {'values': [['New post from social media!']]}  
url = f'https://sheets.googleapis.com/v4/spreadsheets/{spreadsheet_id}/values/{range_name}:append?valueInputOption=RAW'
headers = {'Authorization': 'Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN', 'Content-Type': 'application/json'}

request = urllib.request.Request(url, data=json.dumps(data).encode('utf-8'), headers=headers)
response = urllib.request.urlopen(request)
response_data = response.read().decode('utf-8')
print(response_data)
if response.status != 200:
    print('Error appending data to Google Sheets')

steps.technical_explanation: Use the GitHub API to create a repository. Send a POST request to https://api.github.com/user/repos with the necessary headers including Authorization. Handle errors by checking the response status.
steps.code_snippet:
import urllib.request
import json

def create_github_repo(repo_name, token):
    url = 'https://api.github.com/user/repos'
    headers = {'Authorization': f'token {token}', 'Content-Type': 'application/json'}
    data = json.dumps({'name': repo_name}).encode('utf-8')
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, headers=headers)
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as response:
        return json.loads(response.read())

repo_name = 'my-new-repo'
token = 'your_github_token'
response = create_github_repo(repo_name, token)
actions: Create a new GitHub repository using the API.
Store the repository URL for future steps.
Generate a personal access token with repo permissions.

config.description: Personal access token for GitHub API.

checklist: Repository is created successfully.
Repository URL is stored for later use.
steps.expectedResult: A new GitHub repository is created and ready for use.

steps.title: Set Up Sentry for Error Tracking
steps.description: Integrate Sentry with your GitHub repository to track and monitor errors in your code. This setup will help identify and resolve issues promptly.
steps.technical_explanation: To set up Sentry, send a POST request to https://sentry.io/api/projects/ with the correct headers and payload. Ensure to handle any errors returned by the API.
steps.code_snippet:
def create_sentry_project(org_slug, project_name, token):
    url = f'https://sentry.io/api/0/projects/{org_slug}/'
    headers = {'Authorization': f'Bearer {token}', 'Content-Type': 'application/json'}
    data = json.dumps({'name': project_name}).encode('utf-8')
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, headers=headers)
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as response:
        return json.loads(response.read())

org_slug = 'your_org_slug'
project_name = 'my_project'
token = 'your_sentry_token'
response = create_sentry_project(org_slug, project_name, token)

steps.title: Configure Automated Code Quality Checks
steps.description: Implement GitHub Actions to automatically run code quality checks on each pull request. This ensures consistent adherence to coding standards.
steps.technical_explanation: Create a GitHub Actions workflow file that triggers on pull requests. Use the appropriate actions to run linting and testing. Handle any errors by checking the output of the actions.
steps.code_snippet:
workflow_content = '''name: CI
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v2
      - name: Run Lint
        run: python -m flake8 .
''' 

with open('.github/workflows/ci.yml', 'w') as f:
    f.write(workflow_content)
actions: Create a .github/workflows directory in your repository.
Add a CI workflow YAML file to run code quality checks.
Test the workflow by creating a pull request.
